title: Impact of Tobacco Advertising Restrictions in Switzerland: A Quasi-Experimental Study on the Effect of Billboard Bans on Smoking
abstract: arXiv:2601.08352v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This study assesses the impact of tobacco billboard bans on smoking in Switzerland, exploiting their staggered adoption across regions, i.e., the cantons. Based on retrospective smoking histories from the Swiss Health Survey, a panel of individuals' annual smoking status is reconstructed, containing more than one million observations from 1993 to 2017. Estimation relies on staggered difference-in-differences as well as a complementary latent factor model, which relaxes the common trends assumption. The findings indicate that tobacco billboard bans lead to a reduction in smoking rates. Reductions of up to 0.9 percentage points correspond to an approximate 3% decline in the smoking rate. The effect is driven by women and individuals aged 25-44 and 65+. translated_title: 瑞士烟草广告限制的影响：广告牌禁令对吸烟影响的准实验研究
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2601.08352v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：本研究评估了瑞士烟草广告牌禁令对吸烟的影响，利用了各州（即各州）之间逐步实施的时间差异。基于瑞士健康调查的回顾性吸烟史，重建了个人年度吸烟状态的面板数据，包含1993年至2017年间超过一百万条观测。估计依赖于交错差异中的差异以及一个补充的潜在因子模型，该模型放宽了共同趋势假设。研究结果表明，烟草广告牌禁令导致吸烟率下降。下降幅度高达0.9个百分点，相当于吸烟率约3%的降低。该效应主要由女性和25-44岁及65岁以上人群驱动。总体而言，这些证据表明，即使是部分烟草广告禁令，如广告牌禁令，也能有效降低吸烟率，并作为全面政策工具中的有价值组成部分。
tldr: 这项研究通过利用瑞士各州逐步实施广告牌禁令的时间差异，发现烟草广告牌禁令能显著降低吸烟率（约3%），且效果在女性和特定年龄段人群中尤为明显，表明部分广告禁令是有效的政策工具。
en_tdlr: This study exploits staggered billboard ban adoption across Swiss cantons and finds that tobacco billboard bans reduce smoking rates by about 3%, with effects driven by women and specific age groups, indicating partial advertising bans are an effective policy tool.
